correctness.rationale: In R=F_q[x]/(x^p) in characteristic p the derivative is well-defined. Units have one-dimensional commutants by g=fh. For valuation v <=(p-1)/2 a leading coefficient excludes smaller valuations and the condition x^{2v}h′=0 gives exactly v degrees of freedom. For v >=(p+1)/2 the centralizer is exactly x^{p-v+1}R, dimension v-1. There are (q-1)q^{p-v-1} elements in each valuation stratum; summation gives the claimed rank polynomial and q^{p-2}(q^3+(p-1)(q^2-1)/2) commuting pairs. The independent matrix-rank checker exhaustively verifies all p=q=5 elements (3125), 21625 commuting pairs, and 961 further deterministic samples for p=7,11,13. The proof, not these finite samples, establishes all p and q.

value.rationale: The problem asks for the canonical complete adjoint-rank distribution and total rational-point count of the Witt commuting-pair variety across all modular primes and every finite extension. It converts geometric commuting-variety studies into a quantitative finite-field invariant and reveals the two valuation regimes, with a sharp transition at half the characteristic. The answer is neither a bounded parameter table nor an arbitrary numerical slice; it is an exact infinite-family classification. It is potentially useful for finite-field Lie algebra sampling, centralizer distributions and comparisons of modular Cartan-type structures.
